abTest.name: Subject A/B test
abTest.tagline: Find out which subject works best before sending to everyone.

1.title: Part of the audience joins the test
1.text: Half of that part gets subject A and the other half gets subject B.

2.title: Results are measured
2.text: During the chosen window, we count opens or clicks by people per delivered email.

3.title: The winner goes to the rest
3.text: At the end of the window, the rest of the audience gets the subject with the best result.

abTest.footnote: Opens by bots and privacy protections do not count toward choosing the winner.

billing.name: Sending charges
billing.tagline: You pay in batches, each batch before it goes out.

1.title: One batch before it goes out
1.text: Before the first emails go out, we charge a batch of up to 1,000 sends to the balance.

2.title: The next batch when the last one runs out
2.text: Each new batch is charged only when the previous one is used up. If the balance does not cover it, the campaign waits and continues on its own after a top up.

3.title: Refund at the end
3.text: When the campaign ends or is stopped, paid emails that were not sent return to the balance at the price of the batch they were charged in.

guided.name: Guided mode
guided.tagline: The essential fields in five steps, one at a time

1.title: One step at a time
1.text: Identity, model, prompt, WhatsApp and review come in sequence, with an example on every field.

2.title: Basic tools included
2.text: When creating, the agent gets the tools that need no setup. When editing, its current tools are kept.

3.title: Optional template
3.text: Pick a number and an approved template and the agent can send that template.

guided.footnote: Custom tools, knowledge and variables live in complete mode.

complete.name: Complete mode
complete.tagline: Every agent setting, organized in tabs

1.title: Tabs in any order
1.text: General, Conversation, Skills, Knowledge and WhatsApp. Open the one you need and save when you are done.

2.title: Tools your way
2.text: Add each tool, choose where it acts and fill in the ones that need setup.

3.title: Agent knowledge
3.text: Upload files and connect knowledge bases and MCP collections for the agent to consult.

complete.footnote: Prompt variables and the WhatsApp template are here too.

smartSend.name: Smart Send
smartSend.tagline: Wave sending guided by Meta's health signals

1.title: Sends one wave
1.text: Starts with a small part of the list.

2.title: Watches Meta
2.text: Waits for the template and number quality signals and counts the wave's failures.

3.title: Decides the next one
3.text: Healthy, the wave grows. On a warning, it shrinks. On a risk, the campaign pauses or stops and sends an email.

smartSend.footnote: Waves only go out within the send hours. Campaigns without Smart Send send as they do today.

templateInCrm.name: Show template in CRM
templateInCrm.tagline: Records the sent template as a message in the conversation

1.title: The template goes out
1.text: The campaign sends the template to the contact through Meta, as usual.

2.title: Becomes a message
2.text: When on, each accepted send is recorded in the conversation with the template text and its variables filled in.

3.title: Shows in the CRM
3.text: The conversation shows what was sent, even if the contact does not reply.

templateInCrm.footnote: Only applies to sends made while it is on. Earlier sends are not recorded afterwards.

scheduledStart.name: Schedule start
scheduledStart.tagline: The campaign starts on its own at the date and time you choose

1.title: Pick date and time
1.text: In this computer's time, between 5 minutes and 1 year ahead.

2.title: The campaign waits
2.text: Until then, nothing is sent unless you start the campaign manually.

3.title: Starts on its own
3.text: At the set time, the campaign starts as if you had clicked start.

agentKnowledge.name: Search the base on each reply
agentKnowledge.tagline: The agent checks its knowledge bases before replying

1.title: Searches by message
1.text: On every reply, the contact's latest message becomes a search in the bases linked to this agent.

2.title: Picks excerpts
2.text: The excerpts closest to the question are added to the agent's context.

3.title: Replies from them
3.text: The agent uses the excerpts for data like prices, dates and names. If they do not cover the question, it replies normally.

agentKnowledge.footnote: When off, nothing is searched automatically on each reply.

trackLinkClicks.name: Track clicks
trackLinkClicks.tagline: Counts taps on the link button without changing where it goes

1.title: The contact taps
1.text: The button opens a short link from your account instead of the direct address.

2.title: The tap is counted
2.text: The shortener records the click and adds it to the button's CTR.

3.title: On to the destination
3.text: The contact reaches the address you configured right away.

trackLinkClicks.footnote: Changing the link needs a new Meta approval. Untracked buttons show as "not tracked", never as 0%.

advantageAudience.name: Advantage+ audience
advantageAudience.tagline: Meta uses your audience as a suggestion and can go beyond it

1.title: Your audience is a suggestion
1.text: The age, gender and interests you choose become a starting point, not a limit.

2.title: Meta widens it
2.text: It can show the ad to people outside the suggestion when it predicts a better chance of results.

3.title: Age limits
3.text: When on, the minimum age must be between 18 and 25 and the maximum is always 65+.

campaignBudget.name: Advantage+ campaign budget
campaignBudget.tagline: One budget for the campaign, split by Meta across the ad sets

1.title: Budget on the campaign
1.text: You set the amount and the bid strategy on the campaign. The ad sets have no budget of their own.

2.title: Meta splits it
2.text: Meta spreads the amount across the campaign's ad sets and sends more to the one that performs best.

3.title: Off
3.text: Each ad set has its own budget and bid, set in the ad set step.

adSchedule.name: Delivery hours
adSchedule.tagline: The ad only shows on the days and hours you mark

1.title: Mark the grid
1.text: Pick the weekdays and hours when the ad may show. Each slot is at least 1 full hour.

2.title: Outside it, paused
2.text: In the hours you did not mark, Meta does not deliver the ad.

3.title: Viewer's time
3.text: The hours follow the time zone of the person seeing the ad, not the ad account's.

adSchedule.footnote: Only available with a lifetime budget, which needs an end date.

creativeEnhancements.name: Advantage+ creative enhancements
creativeEnhancements.tagline: Meta makes light adjustments to the ad for each place it shows

1.title: Adapts the image
1.text: It can crop or expand the image to fit each placement, such as Stories and Reels.

2.title: Adjusts the text
2.text: It can move your texts to other spots and highlight a phrase from them next to the button.

3.title: The rest stays off
3.text: {brandName} turns off the other features, such as AI backgrounds, text over the image, translation and animation.

publishPaused.name: Publish turned off
publishPaused.tagline: Creates everything on Meta, but only runs once you turn it on

1.title: Created on Meta
1.text: Everything new in this publication is created in your ad account, but stays off.

2.title: Nothing runs
2.text: While off, the ad shows to no one and spends nothing.

3.title: You turn it on later
3.text: Turn it on whenever you want from the manager. Without this option, {brandName} turns everything on as soon as publishing ends.

higherIntentForm.name: Higher intent
higherIntentForm.tagline: A review screen before sending filters out people who are not interested

1.title: Answers the questions
1.text: The person fills in the form as usual, with profile details already filled in by Meta.

2.title: Reviews before sending
2.text: An extra screen shows the answers so they can check them and confirm the submission.

3.title: Fewer, firmer leads
3.text: Fewer leads arrive, but from people who stopped to confirm their details.

higherIntentForm.footnote: The form cannot be edited after it is created. To change this option, create another one.

conversionsApi.name: Send conversions to Meta
conversionsApi.tagline: Your CRM tells Meta when a deal is created or won

1.title: Deal in the CRM
1.text: When a deal is created or won, {brandName} builds the event you turned on below.

2.title: Where it goes
2.text: It goes to the dataset if the deal's conversation came from an ad or a Meta channel. Otherwise to the pixel, with the phone encrypted.

3.title: Every 5 minutes
3.text: Events go out in a batch every 5 minutes, only once per deal and event.

conversionsApi.footnote: Only deals from the last 7 days are sent. When you turn it on, those from these 7 days not yet sent also go.

conversionLead.name: Lead when a deal is created
conversionLead.tagline: Each new deal in the CRM becomes a lead event on Meta

1.title: Deal created
1.text: When a deal is created in the CRM, it joins the queue for the next send.

2.title: Lead event
2.text: Meta receives the LeadSubmitted event, only once per deal.

conversionPurchase.name: Purchase when a deal is won
conversionPurchase.tagline: Each won deal becomes a purchase with value on Meta

1.title: Deal won
1.text: When a deal is marked as won in the CRM, it joins the queue for the next send.

2.title: Purchase event
2.text: Meta receives the Purchase event with the deal's value and currency, only once.

conversionPurchase.footnote: A won deal with no value is not sent.

signMessage.name: Sign
signMessage.tagline: Puts your name at the top of the messages you send

1.title: Turn it on before sending
1.text: Applies to the messages you send while it is on. Your choice is saved in this browser.

2.title: Your name goes on top
2.text: {brandName} puts your user name above the text, followed by a colon. On WhatsApp, the name shows in bold.

3.title: Scheduled ones too
3.text: In a scheduled message, the signature carries the name of whoever scheduled it and is added at send time.

signMessage.footnote: Meta templates go out without a signature.

requiredField.name: Required
requiredField.tagline: Prevents saving a record with this field left blank

1.title: On, it needs a value
1.text: Creating a lead or a deal, or editing its fields, with this field empty is refused until someone fills it in.

2.title: Off, it is optional
2.text: The field can stay blank and the record saves normally.

requiredField.footnote: In a lead import, a new lead still comes in without the field and shows up in the import warnings.

classificationField.name: Use as the lead classification
classificationField.tagline: Highlights this field in the lead list, map and filters

1.title: Becomes a list column
1.text: The lead list gets a column with the option chosen for each lead.

2.title: Colors the map
2.text: The lead map paints each lead with its option's color, unless you pick another field to color by.

3.title: Quick filter
3.text: The filter bar offers the field as a shortcut, with how many leads each option has.

classificationField.footnote: Only one select field can have this role. People who cannot see the field do not see the column or the colors.

whatsappOptIn.name: Agreed to WhatsApp messages
whatsappOptIn.tagline: Records that the lead agreed to receive your messages

1.title: Turn on when they agree
1.text: On save, {brandName} records the consent with the date and the source manual entry. An earlier request not to receive stops applying.

2.title: Flows check the consent
2.text: The consent step in flows follows the path for those who agreed, those who declined or those with no record.

3.title: Turning off records a no
3.text: Turning off a saved consent marks that the lead does not want messages, and campaigns start skipping this lead.

whatsappOptIn.footnote: Turning it on requires the permission to record consent. A received message does not count as consent.

exactOnly.name: Exact position only
exactOnly.tagline: Counts only leads with an exact position in the drawn area

1.title: Applies to the map area
1.text: Shows up when the filter uses a drawn area and changes which leads count as inside it.

2.title: Drops approximate ones
2.text: Leads located only by CEP, neighborhood or city leave the area. Only those with an exact position stay.

3.title: Shows who was left out
3.text: The panel counts the approximate leads left out and lets you list them in the table, also by neighborhood.

autoOpenScreens.name: Open screens automatically
autoOpenScreens.tagline: Takes you straight to the screen Elo points to in a reply

1.title: Elo points to a screen
1.text: When an Elo reply points to a {brandName} screen, a card shows up with an Open button.

2.title: On, the screen opens itself
2.text: During the reply, {brandName} takes you to the screen and keeps the Elo panel open.

3.title: Only screens you can access
3.text: Screens outside your access never open by themselves. Off, only the button shows.

autoOpenScreens.footnote: Your choice is saved in this browser.

companyAcceptsLeads.name: Accepts new leads
companyAcceptsLeads.tagline: Opens or closes this company to new leads

1.title: On, any lead can join
1.text: The lead record lets you pick this company. Each lead belongs to at most one company.

2.title: Off, nobody new joins
2.text: The company shows as closed in the picker and the server refuses anyone who tries to join, even if the switch changes at the same moment.

3.title: Members stay
3.text: Closing removes nobody. The company's leads stay in it and can be taken out at any time.

companyAcceptsLeads.footnote: Switching it needs the permission to edit companies.

customerPortfolio.name: Customer portfolio
customerPortfolio.tagline: Customers who reach you directly, no roulette

1.title: You choose who goes in
1.text: From the conversation or the lead, put the customer in your portfolio. On Instagram and Facebook they are recognized by their profile (@).

2.title: New conversations land with you
2.text: Even when you are offline, a new conversation goes straight to your inbox without the roulette. Conversations that already have an owner stay as they are.

3.title: AI and workflows answer first
3.text: If the channel runs an AI agent or workflow, they reply first. When they hand off to a human, the conversation comes to you.

4.title: One customer, one portfolio
4.text: If the customer is already in a colleague's portfolio, only someone who manages portfolios can move them.

customerPortfolio.footnote: Whoever loses the portfolio permission, conversation access or the conversation's department stops receiving: the customers go back to the roulette until someone moves them.

notificationEmail.name: Notification email
notificationEmail.tagline: Decides whether notices also arrive by email, on top of the bell.

1.title: The notification reaches the bell
1.text: Whoever should know sees it in the bell at the top of the app.

2.title: On, it goes by email too
2.text: Each person gets a copy at their account email.

3.title: Off, it stays in the app
3.text: Nothing is lost: the notice stays in the bell, without email.

notificationEmail.footnote: Critical notifications always go by email, even to people who turned the category off.

notificationDigest.name: Daily email summary
notificationDigest.tagline: Gathers the notices of the day into a single email, at 08:00.

1.title: Notices still reach the bell
1.text: During the day, each notice shows up in the bell right away, as always.

2.title: One email in the morning
2.text: At 08:00 (Brasília time) you get one email with up to 20 notices you have not read yet, and how many were left out.

3.title: What you already read stays out
3.text: Notices read before 08:00 leave the summary. With nothing pending, no email arrives.

notificationDigest.footnote: Critical notifications do not wait for the summary: they arrive by email right away.

adminsInRoulette.name: Admins receive assignments
adminsInRoulette.tagline: Decides whether admins and owners take part in the conversation roulette.

1.title: A conversation arrives
1.text: The roulette picks who receives it among the members who can attend.

2.title: On, admins take part
2.text: Admins and owners receive conversations like any other agent.

3.title: Off, they stay out
3.text: Only the other members receive. Rescue and incoming WhatsApp calls follow the same rule.

rouletteRescue.name: Rescue unattended conversations
rouletteRescue.tagline: Moves on a conversation the agent did not open in time.

1.title: The deadline starts
1.text: When the roulette hands out a conversation, the deadline set below starts counting.

2.title: Nobody opened it
2.text: If the agent neither opens nor replies in time, the conversation goes to the next one in the roulette.

3.title: End of the round
3.text: After up to 5 hand-overs, or one full round, it is left without an owner and visible to everyone.

rouletteRescue.footnote: Only works in the Agents online recently mode. With working hours set, the deadline only runs while the operation is open.

rouletteOnline.name: Only who is online
rouletteOnline.tagline: The roulette only considers people with the dashboard open right now.

1.title: A conversation arrives
1.text: The roulette looks at who is connected at this moment and can receive conversations.

2.title: Offline stays out
2.text: Whoever closed the dashboard is left out, even if they are on the list of who receives.

3.title: Nobody connected
3.text: The conversation stays without an owner, visible to the team, for whoever opens it first.

rouletteLastSeen.name: Who was online recently
rouletteLastSeen.tagline: People who were connected inside the window also join, even if they are away now.

1.title: The window decides
1.text: Whoever was online inside the configured window, from 1 to 168 hours, joins.

2.title: Most recent first
2.text: In round robin, whoever was online most recently comes first in the queue.

3.title: Rescue
3.text: If the person does not open the conversation in time, rescue passes it on, in the order of the way of picking.

rouletteLastSeen.footnote: If nobody was online inside the window, the roulette uses whoever is online now.

rouletteRoundRobin.name: Round robin
rouletteRoundRobin.tagline: One conversation per person, each in turn.

1.title: An ordered queue
1.text: The people available form a queue that repeats.

2.title: Next in turn
2.text: Each conversation goes to whoever comes after the person who got the last one.

3.title: In and out
3.text: Whoever becomes unavailable is skipped, and the queue carries on where it stopped.

roulettePriority.name: Priority tiers
roulettePriority.tagline: You choose who receives and the order in which tiers are called.

1.title: Build the list
1.text: Tick the people who can receive and give each one a tier from 1 to 10.

2.title: Tier 1 first
2.text: Conversations go only to tier 1, in turn among the people in that tier.

3.title: Overflow
3.text: If nobody in tier 1 is available or has room, the next tier starts receiving.

4.title: Nobody on the list
4.text: The conversation stays without an owner and visible to the team. Anyone not on the list never receives through the roulette.

roulettePriority.footnote: With rescue on, an ignored conversation moves to another person in the same tier and then to the next tier.

rouletteWeighted.name: Weighted
rouletteWeighted.tagline: Each person receives a share in proportion to the weight you give.

1.title: Build the list
1.text: Tick who can receive and give each person a weight from 1 to 10.

2.title: Proportional shares
2.text: Weight 3 receives three times as much as weight 1, interleaving conversations instead of sending several in a row to the same person.

3.title: Out of the count
3.text: Whoever is unavailable or at the limit leaves the split until they are back.

rouletteWeighted.footnote: Anyone not on the list never receives through the roulette.

rouletteLeastBusy.name: Least busy
rouletteLeastBusy.tagline: The conversation goes to whoever has the fewest open conversations now.

1.title: Counts what is open
1.text: The roulette adds up each person's conversations that are not finished yet, across every channel.

2.title: Lightest load receives
2.text: Whoever has the fewest open conversations gets the new one.

3.title: Ties
3.text: If two people have the same load, whoever has gone longest without receiving a conversation gets it.

rouletteLeastBusy.footnote: Whoever closes fast receives more. To split by arrival, use Longest without one.

rouletteLongestIdle.name: Longest without one
rouletteLongestIdle.tagline: The conversation goes to whoever has gone longest without receiving one.

1.title: Looks at the last hand-out
1.text: The roulette compares when each person last received a conversation, by any route.

2.title: Longest wait receives
2.text: Whoever never received one, or received one longest ago, comes first.

3.title: Back of the queue
3.text: Whoever just received one goes to the back of the queue.

rouletteRandom.name: Random
rouletteRandom.tagline: Draws who receives among the people available.

1.title: A draw
1.text: Each conversation is drawn among whoever is available, with the same chance for everyone.

2.title: No balance guarantee
2.text: In the short run someone may receive more than the others. To split evenly, use Round robin.

rouletteClaim.name: Open claim
rouletteClaim.tagline: Nobody is picked: the conversation goes to whoever opens it first.

1.title: A conversation arrives
1.text: It comes in without an owner and shows for everyone who can handle it.

2.title: Whoever opens it first
2.text: The first person to open the conversation becomes its owner.

3.title: Automation hand-off
3.text: When automation hands the conversation to a person, it is also left open for the team.

rouletteClaim.footnote: The portfolio still applies, and if someone on the team had already written to the customer in this conversation, it goes back to them.

rouletteCapacity.name: Open conversation limit
rouletteCapacity.tagline: Anyone holding too many open conversations gets no new ones until they free up room.

1.title: Set the limit
1.text: Choose how many open conversations each person may hold, from 1 to 500. With no number, there is no limit.

2.title: Full stays out
2.text: Whoever reached the limit is skipped, whatever the way of picking.

3.title: Everyone at the limit
3.text: The conversation stays without an owner and visible to the team. The customer's next message tries again.

rouletteCapacity.footnote: The portfolio holder receives their customers' conversations even at the limit.

autoCloseIdle.name: Auto-close on customer silence
autoCloseIdle.tagline: Closes the conversation when the customer stops replying.

1.title: We spoke last
1.text: Applies when the last message came from an agent or the AI.

2.title: The customer stays quiet
2.text: After the silence period, from 1 to 168 hours, the conversation is closed with the reason silence.

3.title: Customer spoke last
3.text: Then this rule closes nothing, because it is our turn to reply.

autoCloseIdle.footnote: For now it only applies to official WhatsApp API conversations.

autoCloseMaxAge.name: Auto-close on max age
autoCloseMaxAge.tagline: Closes conversations idle for a long time, on either side.

1.title: Counts from the last message
1.text: The period counts from the last message, whether ours or the customer's.

2.title: Closes for inactivity
2.text: After the period, from 24 to 2160 hours, the conversation is closed with the reason inactivity.

3.title: Keeps the queue clean
3.text: It closes even when the customer spoke last, so forgotten conversations do not pile up.

autoCloseMaxAge.footnote: For now it only applies to official WhatsApp API conversations.

outcomeCapture.name: Collect an outcome
outcomeCapture.tagline: Every closing records how the conversation ended.

1.title: Pick when closing
1.text: Whoever closes picks an outcome from the list: a person on screen, the AI and workflows in Finish conversation.

2.title: Automatic closes get a code
2.text: Automatic system closes get a reserved code without asking anyone.

3.title: Counts from now on
3.text: Counting starts when you turn it on and nothing from the past is judged. The target compares resolving outcomes.

outcomeRequired.name: Require it to finish
outcomeRequired.tagline: Without a chosen outcome, the conversation is not closed.

1.title: On, it blocks
1.text: The conversation only closes with an outcome from the list, whether by a person, the AI or a workflow.

2.title: Off, it is optional
2.text: Whoever closes may skip it. The AI and workflows get a not informed code.

3.title: The system is not blocked
3.text: Automatic closes for silence or inactivity are never stopped.

workingHours.name: Set working hours
workingHours.tagline: Says when the operation is open for conversation rescue.

1.title: Mark days and ranges
1.text: Only the marked days and ranges count as open, in the chosen time zone.

2.title: Rescue follows them
2.text: Outside working hours rescue does not run, and the agent's deadline only runs during open minutes.

3.title: Off
3.text: Without hours, rescue works 24 hours a day. In a department, the workspace hours apply.

workingHours.footnote: In attendance, only rescue uses these hours. They are also Smart Send's default send hours.

channelAutoReply.name: Reply automatically
channelAutoReply.tagline: An AI agent or an automation handles new messages on this channel.

1.title: Choose who attends
1.text: Select an agent or an automation. Switching from one to the other turns replies off.

2.title: Every message triggers
2.text: When on, every new message is answered by the agent or triggers the chosen automation.

3.title: Pause per conversation
3.text: You can pause the automation in a single conversation without changing this setting.

channelAutoReply.footnote: Each channel's rules apply, such as Meta's 24 hour window. On official WhatsApp, campaign conversations follow the campaign.

conversationAnalysis.name: Analyse conversations with AI
conversationAnalysis.tagline: The AI classifies each conversation once it goes quiet.

1.title: Waits for a pause
1.text: A few minutes after the last message, the conversation joins the analysis queue.

2.title: The AI classifies
2.text: The AI reads the conversation and records its classification. It only analyses again after new messages.

3.title: Becomes a metric
3.text: The result shows in Metrics > Audience and in the conversation's analysis card.

conversationAnalysis.footnote: Each analysis is billed. Past the workspace daily limit, analyses wait in the queue and are not lost.

autoStaging.name: Move the stage automatically
autoStaging.tagline: The AI puts the conversation in the funnel stage that fits it now.

1.title: Checks every message
1.text: The AI checks where in the funnel the conversation is right now.

2.title: Moves when sure
2.text: With high confidence it moves at once. Otherwise it decides a few minutes after the conversation stops.

3.title: Describe your stages
3.text: The AI picks among the stages of the conversation's funnel. Clear descriptions help it get it right.

autoMemory.name: Remember facts about the lead
autoMemory.tagline: Keeps what is worth remembering from the conversation in the lead's memory.

1.title: Waits for a pause
1.text: A few minutes after the conversation stops, the AI rereads what was said.

2.title: Keeps what lasts
2.text: It records lasting facts, such as preferences, agreements and dates, in the lead's memory.

3.title: Only with a lead
3.text: Works when the conversation is linked to a lead. Without a lead, nothing is saved.

autoMemory.footnote: Without the minimum AI balance in the workspace, the memory is not updated.

dealAutomation.name: Automatic deals
dealAutomation.tagline: The analysis manages the conversation's deals in a chosen funnel.

1.title: Choose the funnel
1.text: Turn it on and pick a deals funnel. With a single funnel, it is picked for you.

2.title: The AI handles it
2.text: When the conversation stops, the analysis creates, updates and closes the deal, even as won or lost.

3.title: Who owns it
3.text: The conversation owner. Without one, the configured AI agent.

dealAutomation.footnote: Needs a deals funnel in Funnels & stages.

handleGroups.name: Attend groups
handleGroups.tagline: Decides whether automation also acts in WhatsApp groups.

1.title: Groups always arrive
1.text: Group messages show in the inbox whether the switch is on or off.

2.title: On, automation acts
2.text: The agent replies, workflows trigger and analysis runs in groups too.

3.title: Group history
3.text: Importing earlier conversations only brings groups when this option is on.

importHistory.name: Import earlier conversations
importHistory.tagline: Brings the number's recent conversations into the inbox on connect.

1.title: On connect
1.text: When the number connects, {brandName} fetches the recent conversations kept in WhatsApp.

2.title: Arrive already read
2.text: They enter the inbox as read and without triggering automations.

3.title: Off
3.text: Only new messages arrive. Turning it off midway cancels the import in progress.

importHistory.footnote: Only a recent period comes in, not the device's whole history.

whatsappCalling.name: WhatsApp Calling
whatsappCalling.tagline: The team makes and takes voice calls through this number.

1.title: Turns on at Meta
1.text: The switch enables or disables voice calls for this number directly at Meta.

2.title: Team in {brandName}
2.text: With calls enabled, the team calls and answers through {brandName} using this number.

3.title: Who answers
3.text: The call rings the conversation owner. Without an owner, whoever is available.

whatsappCalling.footnote: Meta requires a limit of at least 2,000 conversations per 24 hours on the number.

sipTrunkEnabled.name: Line active
sipTrunkEnabled.tagline: Connects the line to the carrier and puts it in the dialer.

1.title: Active, connects
1.text: The line connects to the carrier, registering when needed, and shows in the dialer.

2.title: The type decides
2.text: Outbound calls need a line of type outbound or bidirectional.

3.title: Inactive, disconnects
3.text: The connection to the carrier is closed and the line makes no calls.

sipSkipRegistration.name: Do not register (by IP)
sipSkipRegistration.tagline: For carriers that allow your IP instead of a username and password.

1.title: Normally, it registers
1.text: By default the line registers with the carrier using a username and password.

2.title: On, by IP
2.text: Nothing is registered and the username is no longer required. The carrier recognizes the server's address.

sipSkipRegistration.footnote: Use it only when the carrier has already allowed the {brandName} server's IP.

sipStun.name: Public address via STUN
sipStun.tagline: Finds the address seen from outside when the server sits behind NAT.

1.title: Asks STUN
1.text: On connect, the line asks a STUN server for the address and port seen from outside.

2.title: Announces it
2.text: That address is the one the carrier uses to reach the line.

3.title: Order of use
3.text: A filled public address takes priority. If STUN fails, the server's public IP is used.

webchatHumanRequest.name: Talk to a person button
webchatHumanRequest.tagline: The visitor can ask for a person while the AI attends.

1.title: Button in the chat
1.text: While the AI attends, the visitor sees the option to ask for a person.

2.title: Goes to the roulette
2.text: The conversation goes to the chat department's roulette and the automation pauses.

3.title: Off
3.text: The visitor stays with the AI, with no way to ask for a person in the chat.

webchatAttachments.name: Allow attachments
webchatAttachments.tagline: The visitor can send files through the website chat.

1.title: On, accepts files
1.text: The visitor attaches files of the accepted types, up to the maximum size.

2.title: Off, text only
2.text: The chat only accepts text messages and refuses any attachment.

webchatActive.name: Chat active
webchatActive.tagline: Shows or pauses the chat on every allowed website.

1.title: Active
1.text: The chat shows and attends on the websites in the allowed list.

2.title: Paused
2.text: It disappears from every website at once. Earlier conversations stay in the inbox.

webchatActive.footnote: Without any allowed website, the chat does not show, even when active.

messengerGetStarted.name: Get Started button
messengerGetStarted.tagline: Shows the Get Started button to anyone opening a new conversation.

1.title: Shows at the start
1.text: Messenger shows the Get Started button to anyone opening a new conversation with the page.

2.title: A tap becomes a message
2.text: The tap reaches the conversation as a message and goes on to the page's automation.

3.title: The menu needs it
3.text: The persistent menu can only be saved with the Get Started button on.

messengerComposerHidden.name: Hide the text field
messengerComposerHidden.tagline: People talk only through the persistent menu, without typing.

1.title: Menu only
1.text: When on, Messenger hides the text field and people use only the persistent menu items.

2.title: Per language
2.text: Applies to the menu of the language being edited. Each language has its own option.

sendCapRemove.name: Remove the limit
sendCapRemove.tagline: Removes the monthly send ceiling for this workspace.

1.title: Deletes the limit
1.text: The workspace's monthly limit is removed together with the cycle's count.

2.title: Sends without a ceiling
2.text: Meta billed templates no longer have a monthly ceiling. Balance and Meta rules still apply.

3.title: Needs the code
3.text: Removing only works with a super admin's personal unlock code.

alertSound.name: Alert sound
alertSound.tagline: A short sound tells you something arrived, without looking at the screen.

1.title: Something new arrived
1.text: A customer message, a team message or a bell notification.

2.title: On, a sound plays
2.text: Customers have one sound, the team and notifications have another. Many messages at once play once.

3.title: Off, visual only
3.text: Counters and alerts stay on screen; only the sound goes away.

desktopAlerts.name: Desktop alerts
desktopAlerts.tagline: The alert shows in the corner of the screen even with the platform in another tab.

1.title: You're in another tab
1.text: Or in another program, with the platform open in the background.

2.title: On, the computer alerts you
2.text: One alert per chat: a new one replaces the old one. Many at once become a summary.

3.title: Click to open
3.text: The click brings the platform to the front, on the right chat or notification.

desktopAlerts.footnote: The browser asks for your permission once. With several tabs open, only one shows each alert.

teamChatMute.name: Mute chat
teamChatMute.tagline: For busy groups: messages arrive without calling for your attention.

1.title: Messages keep arriving
1.text: Everything stays in the history and you read it when you want.

2.title: No sound and no alert
2.text: The chat leaves the counter on the Team button.

3.title: Mentions still alert
3.text: If someone mentions you with @, the alert arrives as usual.

postSchedule.name: Schedule
postSchedule.tagline: Sets the post to go out on its own later

1.title: Pick date and time
1.text: From 10 minutes to 75 days ahead. Videos accept up to 180 days.

2.title: Facebook publishes
2.text: The post is scheduled on the Page itself and goes out on its own at the set time.

3.title: Extras ready too
3.text: Comment automation and analysis turned on here already apply to the scheduled post.

postCommentRule.name: Comment automation
postCommentRule.tagline: Creates a rule that answers whoever comments on this post

1.title: Set the trigger
1.text: Any comment, or only those that contain or exactly match the chosen words. Accents and capitals are ignored.

2.title: Pick the actions
2.text: Reply publicly, message privately (Messenger or Direct) and hide. On Facebook, also like or delete.

3.title: Starts on publish
3.text: The rule is created active right after the post goes out and acts only on its new comments.

postCommentRule.footnote: Meta allows a single private message per comment. The conversation it opens shows up in the inbox.

postAnalysis.name: Analysis for this post
postAnalysis.tagline: Adjusts comment analysis for this post only

1.title: Off, it inherits
1.text: The post follows the analysis settings of the account or Page.

2.title: On, adjust what you want
2.text: Turn analysis on or off, change model, severity threshold or topics, and write instructions just for it.

3.title: Blank inherits
3.text: An empty field keeps coming from the account. Instructions here add to the account's, they do not replace them.

postAnalysis.footnote: Turning analysis on here works even when the account's analysis is off. Each analysed comment is billed as AI usage.

postOwnTopics.name: Own topics
postOwnTopics.tagline: Classifies this post's comments with a topic list of its own

1.title: Off, it inherits
1.text: Comments on this post are classified with the account's topics.

2.title: On, its own list
2.text: The topics you write replace the account's list on this post. An empty list keeps inheriting.

3.title: Other always exists
3.text: Comments that fit no topic go to Other.

commentRuleEnabled.name: Rule active
commentRuleEnabled.tagline: Turns the rule on or pauses it without losing its setup

1.title: Checks every comment
1.text: When active, the rule is tested on each new comment from other people. The account's own and hidden comments are left out.

2.title: Only the first acts
2.text: One rule acts per comment. Rules for the post are tested before general ones and, within each, oldest first.

3.title: Paused stays saved
3.text: When off, the rule is ignored but kept. Comments that arrived during the pause are not answered later.

commentRuleScope.name: Only on this post
commentRuleScope.tagline: Sets whether the rule applies to one post or to all of them

1.title: On: this one only
1.text: The rule only answers comments on this post.

2.title: Off: every post
2.text: The rule applies to every post of the account or Page, including future ones.

3.title: Order between rules
3.text: When several rules match, the ones for this post are tested before the general ones.

commentAnalysis.name: Comment analysis
commentAnalysis.tagline: AI classifies each new comment on this account's posts

1.title: A comment arrives
1.text: Each new comment from other people joins the queue. The account's own comments are left out.

2.title: AI classifies it
2.text: It assigns topic, stance and severity using the model, topics and instructions on this screen.

3.title: Cost with a cap
3.text: Each analysis is billed to the balance as AI usage. Once the daily maximum is hit, it pauses until the next day.

4.title: Off stops at once
4.text: When off, nothing new joins the queue and whatever was pending is no longer analysed.

commentAnalysis.footnote: Each post can turn analysis on or off just for itself in the post's Analysis tab.

alertRuleEnabled.name: Alert rule active
alertRuleEnabled.tagline: Notifies you on WhatsApp when the analysis crosses the rule's limit

1.title: Watches the analysis
1.text: When active, the rule checks new analysis results against the limit you set.

2.title: Notifies on WhatsApp
2.text: Once the limit is crossed, it sends the notice to the chosen number, over the official or unofficial channel.

3.title: No flood
3.text: It respects the interval between notices and the daily maximum. When off, the rule stays saved and sends nothing.

alertRuleEnabled.footnote: Without a connected number on the chosen channel, the rule cannot be turned on. On the official channel, each notice uses balance.

alertBrief.name: Include the AI reading
alertBrief.tagline: Adds a short reading of what is happening to the notice

1.title: The alert fires
1.text: When the rule crosses its limit, the notice is built as usual.

2.title: AI reads the case
2.text: It writes one sentence on what is happening and another on how to respond.

3.title: Billed per alert
3.text: Each reading is a billed AI call. If the AI fails, the notice goes out without it.

alertBrief.footnote: On official WhatsApp, the reading only shows if the approved template has a variable for it.

required.name: Required
required.tagline: The person only moves on after answering this question

1.title: On, asks for the answer
1.text: WhatsApp does not let the person go to the next screen with this question blank.

2.title: Off, it is optional
2.text: The question shows as optional and can be skipped. To branch screens on the answer, the question must be required.

sensitive.name: Sensitive data
sensitive.tagline: Hides this answer from anyone without permission to see sensitive data

1.title: Hidden in the WhatsApp summary
1.text: Meta does not show the value in the summary the person sees after submitting the form.

2.title: Masked in the conversation
2.text: In the conversation history, the AI and the analyses, the answer shows as ••••.

3.title: Full only with permission
3.text: In the response list and the export, the full value shows only to those who can see sensitive answers.

sensitive.footnote: Photos and documents are always treated as sensitive.

ladder.name: Sending levels
ladder.tagline: Your account earns limit and reputation as it sends well

1.title: Evaluation
1.text: You start on a shared subdomain that is ready to use, with a lower daily limit, while mailbox providers get to know your sending.

2.title: Trusted
2.text: After a trouble free period, with enough deliveries and few bounces and complaints, the account moves to a subdomain with a better reputation.

3.title: Own domain
3.text: Once your company's domain is connected, emails go out from it, with no daily limit. On a new domain, raise your volume gradually over the first few weeks.

ladder.footnote: Bounces and complaints over the limit can pause sending at any level.

dnsRecords.name: DNS records
dnsRecords.tagline: What each record does for your domain

1.title: DKIM
1.text: Signs each email so providers know it came from you and was not changed on the way.

2.title: Bounces (MAIL FROM)
2.text: A subdomain just for receiving notices about undelivered emails, with an SPF record that authorizes sending.

3.title: Replies
3.text: An MX on a replies subdomain brings what your contacts answer straight into the inbox.

4.title: DMARC
4.text: Tells providers how to treat emails that fail verification. Created only if the domain does not have one yet.

dnsRecords.footnote: No existing record changes: the main domain's MX, which delivers your current mailbox, stays the same.

webhookEnabled.name: Active webhook
webhookEnabled.tagline: Your system learns about every email right away

1.title: Event
1.text: When an API email is delivered, bounced, opened or clicked, the event is prepared for every webhook that chose it.

2.title: Signed delivery
2.text: The event reaches your address by POST, signed with the webhook secret.

3.title: Retries
3.text: Without a 2xx answer, the delivery is repeated at growing intervals for about 10 hours.

webhookEnabled.footnote: When paused, the webhook receives no new events; it is never paused on its own.

fixImportTypos.name: Fix typos
fixImportTypos.tagline: Mistyped domains become the right domain before they reach your base

1.title: Check
1.text: During the dry run, each e-mail is compared with the most used providers, such as Gmail, Hotmail, Outlook, Yahoo, UOL, BOL, Terra, IG and Globo.

2.title: Suggestion
2.text: A domain one letter away from one of them, such as gmial.com, gets the right domain as a suggestion.

3.title: Fix
3.text: With the option on, the lead is imported with the corrected address. With it off, the e-mail goes in as it came and the warning stays in the rows file.

fixImportTypos.footnote: Short domains and real domains that look like a provider get no suggestion, so a correct address is never changed.

dropUndeliverableImport.name: Import without e-mails that cannot receive
dropUndeliverableImport.tagline: Addresses that will never receive stay out of your base from the import on

1.title: Check
1.text: During the dry run, each domain is looked up once, and the addresses are compared with the disposable e-mail list and with those that already bounced as nonexistent.

2.title: Out of the base
2.text: With the option on, these leads come in without the e-mail; the rest of the record is imported as usual.

3.title: Clean campaigns
3.text: Even with it off, no campaign sends to these addresses: the review shows each one with its reason.

dropUndeliverableImport.footnote: Addresses on your block list stay on the lead, because the block records the person's decision.

carrierMarketing.name: Marketing message
carrierMarketing.tagline: Applies the RCS and SMS marketing rules to this send

1.title: On, respects who left
1.text: Leads who asked to leave and contacts who replied SAIR on RCS or SMS do not receive it.

2.title: On, hours and limit
2.text: Sends only within the send hours and up to the message limit per contact. Outside the hours, the node takes Failed with the next opening.

3.title: Off, service message
3.text: For order confirmations and payment notices. Only blocked contacts are refused.

requiredColumn.name: Required
requiredColumn.tagline: The row is only written with this column filled

1.title: On, the column is demanded
1.text: The agent asks the customer before recording, and a workflow without this value takes the error output.

2.title: Off, it can stay blank
2.text: The row is written even with no value in this column.

archivedColumn.name: Archived
archivedColumn.tagline: The column stops receiving values and its history stays in the spreadsheet

1.title: On, it leaves the tools
1.text: Agents, workflows and your team stop filling this column.

2.title: The history stays
2.text: The column stays in Google with the values already written. Nothing is deleted.

3.title: Off, it receives again
3.text: Unarchive whenever you want and the column is filled again.

signing.title: How to verify the signature
signing.description: Each delivery carries these headers. Recompute the HMAC with the secret and compare before trusting the body.
signing.retries: Answer with any 2xx code to confirm. Without confirmation, the delivery is repeated after 30 s, 2 min, 10 min, 30 min, 1 h, 3 h and 6 h. If the address fails for more than an hour, whoever configures email gets a notice; the webhook is never paused on its own.
